title: TACE responser NDRG1 acts as a guardian against ferroptosis in HCC
author: Tang, Wang, et al.

steps.title: Acquire public transcriptomic datasets
steps.instruction: Download the HCC microarray datasets GSE14520 and GSE104580 from the GEO database (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/) and obtain mRNA‑sequencing data from the ICGC database (https://dcc.icgc.org/) and the TCGA database (https://www.cancer.gov/about-nci/organization/ccg/research/structural-genomics/tcga).

steps.title: Identify differentially expressed genes
steps.instruction: Use the limma R package to perform differential expression analysis on the HCC patients, applying a corrected P value of 1 as the significance threshold; generate Venn diagrams to retain DEGs shared between the GSE14520 and GSE104580 cohorts for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Perform functional enrichment analysis
steps.instruction: Submit the shared DEGs to the Metascape online tool (http://metascape.org) for KEGG and GO enrichment; consider results with an adjusted p value < 0.05 as statistically significant.

steps.title: Conduct consensus clustering
steps.instruction: Apply the R package "ConsensusClusterPlus" to the shared DEGs, testing k values from 2 to 9 with 1000 iterations per k; create a consistency matrix for each k, select the optimal matrix based on the consistency distribution, and define TACE‑response molecular subtypes. Then use the R package "survminer" to draw Kaplan–Meier curves comparing survival between subgroups.

steps.title: Run GSVA and GSEA pathways analysis
steps.instruction: Execute GSVA with the R package "GSVA" on the DEGs; obtain immune‑related gene sets from ImmPort (https://www.immport.org/home) and metabolism‑related sets from MSigDB (http://software.broadinstitute.org/gsea/msigdb). Perform GSEA, accepting pathways with adjusted p values = 1, nominal (NOM) p < 0.05 and FDR q‑value < 0.25.

steps.title: Identify core gene with random forest
steps.instruction: Use the R package "randomForestSRC" on the GSE14520 cohort: bootstrap‑sample n cases to build n survival trees, randomly select a subset of covariates at each node, compute out‑of‑bag (OOB) error rates for different parameter combinations, choose the combination that minimizes overall error, and calculate variable importance (VIMP) for each predictor.

steps.title: Culture liver cancer cell lines
steps.instruction: Maintain human HCC cell lines SK‑HEP1 and HCC‑LM3 in a humidified incubator set to 37 °C with 5 % CO₂ and 95 % relative humidity.

steps.title: Live/Dead cell staining (Calcein‑AM/PI)
steps.instruction: Prepare staining solution by adding 20 µl Calcein‑AM and 5 µl propidium iodide (PI) to 10 ml DMEM without FBS; mix well and keep protected from light. Wash cultured cells 2–3 times with pre‑warmed PBS at 37 °C, then add 1 ml of the Calcein‑AM/PI mixture. Incubate in a 37 °C CO₂ incubator for 10–15 min, aspirate the solution, wash cells 3–5 times, add 1 ml complete DMEM, and observe fluorescence under a microscope.

steps.title: Immunohistochemical staining of tissue sections
steps.instruction: Section paraffin‑embedded tumor and adjacent normal liver tissue at 4 µm, dry the slides, de‑wax through xylene and graded ethanol, then immerse sections in 3 % H₂O₂ for 20–30 min. Block at room temperature for 1 h, add primary antibody dropwise and incubate overnight at 4 °C. After PBS washes, incubate with avidin/biotinylated HRP for 2 h, develop with DAB chromogen, cover with neutral resin, and air‑dry overnight in a fume hood before microscopic imaging.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of experimental data
steps.instruction: Analyze all experimental results using GraphPad Prism 9 (version 8.0.2) and R software (version 3.6.3); present data as mean ± SEM, consider adjusted P values < 0.05 statistically significant, and repeat each experiment independently three times.
